matrix: Two Major clarifiers: demonstrate the implemented limit and flag any conflict with Chas's approved rule.
notes: Option B, approved by Chas on 7 Nov and confirmed by Si Aye / Chas the same day (not reopened). Major original + two Major clarifiers: the seeker draws one Clarity card, at random from the unused Minor Arcana, then the rule stops (B01, B07, B06). Minor original + two Major clarifiers: no Clarity card, and the two-clarifier limit is stated on the page (B09, added 9 Nov after Deep found this case not demonstrated). At most two clarifiers per card.

rubric.orientation: Each card is read with the meaning for its orientation (upright or reversed text from the card data below), and a reversed card is not merely the negation of its upright meaning.
rubric.position: The position lens names this position and reads the card through the position’s defined meaning (see the table), without drifting in time or role.
rubric.neighbours: The "wider spread" line relates the card to its pair partner (Celtic Cross) or neighbour (other spreads) without inventing a connection the data does not support.
rubric.clarifier1: Clarifier 1 is read as modifying the original card ("how it modifies the original card"), naming both, not as a separate definition.
rubric.clarifier2: Clarifier 2 develops the relationship between both earlier cards, naming all three.
rubric.synthesis: "Together" is a synthesis of the cards, not a list; revisions are shown (Revision 1 kept readable when Clarifier 2 arrives; Revision 2 when the Clarity card arrives).
rubric.clarity: Option B (approved 7 Nov): a Clarity card appears only when the original and both clarifiers are Major, is a Minor not already in the reading, and is read as grounding the three Major cards; a Minor original with two Major clarifiers gets none and the limit is stated.
rubric.max: Max’s lines are the reading’s own words (quoted), in reading order; before Finish he invites and does not sign off; after Finish the closing comes once.
rubric.failure: Deep’s six failure modes: templating, positional drift, reverse-as-opposite, parallel clarification, concatenation instead of synthesis, numerical/symbolic overreach.

positions.label: Guidance
positions.meaning: the guidance you can put into practice today
positions.clarityText:
4 · CLARITY CARD · WHERE THE THREE MAJOR CARDS LAND
Clarity card · Three of Pentacles, reversed

The work may be suffering from unclear roles or dismissed expertise. Agree on a common standard and address a specific skill or communication gap before assigning blame.

Astrology: Earth · Pentacles · Earth

Number: 3

Three develops expression, growth and the effects of working together. In Three of Pentacles, consider how this relates to craft.

Looking closer: A craftsperson discusses a building with two figures who hold a plan.

Three of Pentacles (reversed) modifies Death, and brings the three Major Arcana cards down to an everyday level.

In Guidance, after Death, The Tower and Judgement, the theme of poor coordination and undervalued work points to where this may show up day to day: work, money, body and the material world.

Read this way because Water and Earth are friendly elements, but Three of Pentacles is reversed; drawn at random from the unused Minor Arcana, because the original card and both clarifiers are Major Arcana (Chas’s teaching rule, Option B).

Because Three of Pentacles (reversed) is reversed, it may point to what is blocked, delayed or turned inward in this theme.

positions.original:
1 · THE ORIGINAL CARD IN THIS POSITION
Original Card · XIII · Death

Guidance

CARD CORRESPONDENCE
Scorpio
SKY AT THIS READING
No planetary placement assigned

Astrology: Scorpio · Water

Number: 13

Thirteen transforms a completed form so that another stage can begin. In Death, consider how this relates to transition.

Transition
Release
Renewal

Position: Guidance — Death. Your next step is to work consciously with transition, release, renewal. Choose one practical response you can try, then notice whether it helps.

An ending or change of form asks you to release what has completed its purpose. Make room to grieve and attend to what remains alive; this card speaks symbolically of transition, not a prediction of physical death.

Looking closer: A skeletal rider passes people of different stations as the sun appears between towers. The scene links unavoidable change with the possibility of another beginning.
positions.clar1:
2 · CLARIFIER 1 · HOW IT MODIFIES THE ORIGINAL CARD
Clarifier 1 · XVI · The Tower

A sudden change or unwelcome truth may expose a structure that could not hold. Attend first to immediate support and practical needs, then decide what deserves rebuilding on more honest foundations.

Astrology: Mars · Fire

Number: 16

Sixteen breaks a familiar structure and exposes the foundations beneath it. In The Tower, consider how this relates to disruption.

Looking closer: Lightning strikes a crowned tower and figures fall from it. The image shows the collapse of assumed security, without specifying a literal future event.

The Tower challenges Death.

In Guidance, the theme of disruption and revelation pushes against transition and release; ask what needs balancing before you act.

Read this way because Water and Fire are contrary elements.
positions.clar2:
3 · CLARIFIER 2 · HOW IT DEVELOPS THE RELATIONSHIP BETWEEN BOTH
Clarifier 2 · XX · Judgement

An honest review of the past can help you answer a new sense of purpose. Recognise what you have learned, make amends where possible, and choose the responsibility you are ready to accept now.

Astrology: Fire · Fire

Number: 20

Twenty reviews the journey and invites a more conscious response to its meaning. In Judgement, consider how this relates to awakening.

Looking closer: Figures rise toward an angel sounding a trumpet. The image suggests a summons to awareness and renewal rather than a final verdict on a person.

Judgement challenges Death and reinforces The Tower.

In Guidance, it sides with the first clarifier: the theme of awakening and review builds on disruption (The Tower), while asking what in transition (Death) needs to change.

Read this way because with Death: Water and Fire are contrary elements; with The Tower: both are Fire cards.

Clarifier 2 was drawn because Clarifier 1 is also a Major Arcana card (Chas's teaching rule).
positions.together:
5 · WHAT THEY MEAN TOGETHER
Together in Guidance

Revision 3 · updated when the Clarity card was drawn. The readings above are unchanged.

Death sets the theme in Guidance: transition and release. The Tower pushes back, setting disruption against transition; that friction is part of the message. Judgement sides with The Tower, carrying disruption forward through awakening and asking what in transition has to change. Three of Pentacles (reversed) grounds all three in work, money, body and the material world: in everyday terms, this is likely to show up as poor coordination and undervalued work. As guidance, the cards point to transition giving way to disruption, with awakening pushing that change on, landing day to day as poor coordination. Be ready to let disruption lead; transition is where the change is needed. Three of Pentacles is reversed, so its part in this is weaker, delayed or turned inward.

This is a perspective for reflection, not a fixed prediction.

Death + The Tower + Judgement + Three of Pentacles, reversed

cardData.name: Death
cardData.upright: An ending or change of form asks you to release what has completed its purpose. Make room to grieve and attend to what remains alive; this card speaks symbolically of transition, not a prediction of physical death.
cardData.reversed: Holding tightly to an exhausted arrangement may prolong uncertainty. Ask what you fear losing, then consider a smaller, supported act of release rather than forcing yourself to change all at once.

cardData.name: The Tower
cardData.upright: A sudden change or unwelcome truth may expose a structure that could not hold. Attend first to immediate support and practical needs, then decide what deserves rebuilding on more honest foundations.
cardData.reversed: You may sense instability while trying to prevent any visible change. Take the warning signs seriously and make manageable repairs rather than waiting until the strain demands an emergency response.

cardData.name: Judgement
cardData.upright: An honest review of the past can help you answer a new sense of purpose. Recognise what you have learned, make amends where possible, and choose the responsibility you are ready to accept now.
cardData.reversed: Harsh self-criticism or fear of change may be drowning out a useful inner call. Distinguish responsibility from punishment and take one concrete step instead of waiting to feel fully worthy.

cardData.name: Three of Pentacles
cardData.upright: A shared task benefits from distinct skills and practical feedback. Clarify roles, respect the knowledge each person brings and let the quality of the work grow through cooperation.
cardData.reversed: The work may be suffering from unclear roles or dismissed expertise. Agree on a common standard and address a specific skill or communication gap before assigning blame.

cardData.name: Death
cardData.upright: An ending or change of form asks you to release what has completed its purpose. Make room to grieve and attend to what remains alive; this card speaks symbolically of transition, not a prediction of physical death.
cardData.reversed: Holding tightly to an exhausted arrangement may prolong uncertainty. Ask what you fear losing, then consider a smaller, supported act of release rather than forcing yourself to change all at once.

cardData.name: The Tower
cardData.upright: A sudden change or unwelcome truth may expose a structure that could not hold. Attend first to immediate support and practical needs, then decide what deserves rebuilding on more honest foundations.
cardData.reversed: You may sense instability while trying to prevent any visible change. Take the warning signs seriously and make manageable repairs rather than waiting until the strain demands an emergency response.

cardData.name: Judgement
cardData.upright: An honest review of the past can help you answer a new sense of purpose. Recognise what you have learned, make amends where possible, and choose the responsibility you are ready to accept now.
cardData.reversed: Harsh self-criticism or fear of change may be drowning out a useful inner call. Distinguish responsibility from punishment and take one concrete step instead of waiting to feel fully worthy.

4 · CLARITY CARD · WHERE THE THREE MAJOR CARDS LAND
Clarity card · Five of Cups

Give a disappointment its proper weight without making it the whole picture. Grief and remaining support can coexist; acknowledge the loss, then notice who or what is still available.

Astrology: Water · Cups · Water

Number: 5

Five disrupts an established pattern and invites a response to change. In Five of Cups, consider how this relates to grief.

Looking closer: A cloaked figure looks at three spilled cups while two stand behind, with a bridge nearby.

Five of Cups reinforces Death, and brings the three Major Arcana cards down to an everyday level.

In Guidance, after Death, The Tower and Judgement, the theme of grief and disappointment points to where this may show up day to day: feelings and relationships.

Read this way because both are Water cards; drawn at random from the unused Minor Arcana, because the original card and both clarifiers are Major Arcana (Chas’s teaching rule, Option B).

Death (13) · The Tower (16) · Judgement (20) · Five of Cups (5). Their numbered cards sum to 54, reducing to 9. No opening dice were rolled for this reading.

These numbers are symbolic prompts, not guarantees. Notice whether any patterns resonate with numbers personally meaningful to you.

Take what resonates, and leave the rest.

cardData.name: Death
cardData.upright: An ending or change of form asks you to release what has completed its purpose. Make room to grieve and attend to what remains alive; this card speaks symbolically of transition, not a prediction of physical death.
cardData.reversed: Holding tightly to an exhausted arrangement may prolong uncertainty. Ask what you fear losing, then consider a smaller, supported act of release rather than forcing yourself to change all at once.

cardData.name: The Tower
cardData.upright: A sudden change or unwelcome truth may expose a structure that could not hold. Attend first to immediate support and practical needs, then decide what deserves rebuilding on more honest foundations.
cardData.reversed: You may sense instability while trying to prevent any visible change. Take the warning signs seriously and make manageable repairs rather than waiting until the strain demands an emergency response.

cardData.name: Judgement
cardData.upright: An honest review of the past can help you answer a new sense of purpose. Recognise what you have learned, make amends where possible, and choose the responsibility you are ready to accept now.
cardData.reversed: Harsh self-criticism or fear of change may be drowning out a useful inner call. Distinguish responsibility from punishment and take one concrete step instead of waiting to feel fully worthy.

cardData.name: Five of Cups
cardData.upright: Give a disappointment its proper weight without making it the whole picture. Grief and remaining support can coexist; acknowledge the loss, then notice who or what is still available.
cardData.reversed: Acceptance may be growing, or regret may be repeating without bringing new understanding. Reach toward the support that remains and let moving forward include, rather than erase, the loss.

Original Card · 0 · The Fool

Present Situation

CARD CORRESPONDENCE
Uranus
SKY AT THIS READING

Number: 0

Zero is pure potential: the circle before the first mark, the unformed field from which every number emerges. In a reading it can amplify openness, uncertainty and the possibility of beginning again.

New Beginnings
Innocence
Trust

Position: Present Situation — The Fool. Here, a willingness to begin before every answer is known is a lens for the central situation as you experience it now. Identify one concrete example in your situation and consider how it shapes your response.

The Fool is the moment before experience hardens into certainty: openness, curiosity and the courage to move without needing every answer first. Upright, it favours a fresh beginning approached with alertness rather than fear. In a reading, this may describe a new chapter, an unfamiliar choice, or the feeling that life is asking you to move before every detail is known. In a Past position it can reflect the leap that brought you here; in the Present, a threshold you are standing at now; in the Future, an emerging possibility rather than a guaranteed event.

Looking closer: Notice the white rose and the bright sky. The rose invites sincerity of intention while the bright sky suggests room to think clearly before stepping ahead.

Circumstances are moving through a turn in the cycle. Notice what is changing beyond your control and use the choices still available; an opening becomes useful when preparation meets timing.

Number: 10

Ten completes a cycle and carries its consequences into another beginning. In Wheel of Fortune, consider how this relates to change.

Looking closer: A great wheel turns among symbolic creatures while figures rise and fall around it. Movement and recurrence sit alongside the search for enduring understanding.

Wheel of Fortune supports The Fool.

In Present Situation, the theme of change and cycles can help new beginnings and innocence find a constructive outlet.

Read this way because Air and Fire are friendly elements.

Clarifier 2 · XI · Justice

Look carefully at evidence, agreements and consequences. A balanced decision requires honesty about your own part as well as the other side; make the choice you can explain and take responsibility for.

Astrology: Libra · Air

Number: 11

Eleven asks for conscious judgement as an established order is examined. In Justice, consider how this relates to fairness.

Looking closer: A seated figure holds scales and an upright sword. Consideration and clear judgement must work together, with consequences following the decision.

Justice reinforces The Fool and supports Wheel of Fortune.

In Present Situation, it draws the original card and the first clarifier together: the theme of fairness and accountability gives new beginnings (The Fool) and change (Wheel of Fortune) a shared direction.

Sensual Pleasure
Nurture

Position: Recent Past — The Empress. This may describe how steady care that gives a relationship, project or part of yourself room to grow shaped the path to your current situation. Consider what you want to carry forward and what belongs to an earlier chapter.

4 · CLARITY CARD · WHERE THE THREE MAJOR CARDS LAND
Clarity card · King of Pentacles

Use experience and resources to create dependable conditions for yourself and others. Mature stewardship values maintenance, fair responsibility and a result that can last beyond a single achievement.

Astrology: Earth · Pentacles · Earth

Court rank: King

King is a court role, not a numbered pip card: a directing, accountable expression of the suit’s qualities. It can describe an approach or quality in anyone, without prescribing age or gender.

Looking closer: A king rests with a pentacle and sceptre amid vines, bull imagery and a substantial estate.

King of Pentacles modifies The Emperor, and brings the three Major Arcana cards down to an everyday level.

In Conscious Focus, after The Emperor, The Tower and The Star, the theme of stewardship and stability points to where this may show up day to day: work, money, body and the material world.

Read this way because Fire and Earth are neutral to each other; drawn at random from the unused Minor Arcana, because the original card and both clarifiers are Major Arcana (Chas’s teaching rule, Option B).

As a court card (King), King of Pentacles may describe a person involved, or a way of behaving you could adopt.

THE GOLDEN THREAD
Read the spread as a whole

The Golden Thread follows 32 revealed cards across this reading, including every clarifier and Clarity card. 6 cards came up reversed and are read through their reversed meaning.

PRESENT SITUATION
The Fool + Wheel of Fortune + Justice + Seven of Wands

What is active now is new beginnings, with real momentum behind it from change and fairness, landing day to day as conviction.

CROSSING CHALLENGE
The Magician, reversed + The Hanged Man + Ace of Cups

The obstacle here is manipulation giving way to perspective, with openness pushing that change on. With The Magician reversed, the theme itself is under strain, and The Hanged Man and Ace of Cups show where it can be steadied.

FOUNDATION
The High Priestess + Death, reversed + Temperance + Seven of Pentacles, reversed

What shaped this situation was intuition and clinging both called into question by integration, landing day to day as impatience. Death and Seven of Pentacles are reversed, so their part in this is weaker, delayed or turned inward.

RECENT PAST
The Empress + The Devil + Two of Wands

What shaped this situation was abundance, expressed through attachment and planning.

CONSCIOUS FOCUS
The Emperor + The Tower + The Star + King of Pentacles

Your hopes and fears here gather around authority, with real momentum behind it from disruption and hope, landing day to day as stewardship.

NEAR FUTURE
The Hierophant + Page of Pentacles

If the present course continues, this points toward tradition, with real momentum behind it from study; it is a direction, not a fixed outcome.

YOUR APPROACH
The Lovers, reversed + The Moon, reversed + Five of Swords

The stance the cards describe here is misalignment, expressed through emerging clarity and conflict. With most of these cards reversed, this is more held back or resisted than openly expressed; start with what is blocking it.

SURROUNDING INFLUENCES
The Chariot + Six of Cups

What is active now is direction, with real momentum behind it from memory.

HOPES AND FEARS
Strength + The Sun + Judgement, reversed + Queen of Pentacles

Your hopes and fears here gather around courage, expressed through vitality and self-criticism, landing day to day as practical care. Judgement is reversed, so its part in this is weaker, delayed or turned inward.

POTENTIAL OUTCOME
The Hermit + The World + Nine of Pentacles

If the present course continues, this points toward reflection, with real momentum behind it from completion and independence; it is a direction, not a fixed outcome.

FROM CARD TO CARD

The reading begins with The Fool in Present Situation and moves toward The Hermit in Potential Outcome.

Crossing Challenge · The Magician, reversed. After The Fool, The Magician (reversed) shifts the thread from new beginnings toward manipulation. Reversed, it shows that next step held back or turned inward.

Foundation · The High Priestess. After The Magician (reversed), The High Priestess shifts the thread from manipulation toward intuition. Upright, it offers a way through the difficulty in The Magician (reversed).

Recent Past · The Empress. After The High Priestess, The Empress gives intuition somewhere to go, turning it toward abundance. RESONATE's card notes link these two: The Priestess senses what is forming; The Empress gives it body, care and material expression.

Conscious Focus · The Emperor. After The Empress, The Emperor shifts the thread from abundance toward authority. RESONATE's card notes link these two: The Empress grows and nourishes; The Emperor defines and protects. Together they ask what conditions allow something valuable to endure.

Near Future · The Hierophant. After The Emperor, The Hierophant shifts the thread from authority toward tradition.

Your Approach · The Lovers, reversed. The Lovers (reversed) turns against The Hierophant, setting misalignment against tradition: a turning point in the reading. Reversed, it shows that next step held back or turned inward.

Surrounding Influences · The Chariot. After The Lovers (reversed), The Chariot shifts the thread from misalignment toward direction. Upright, it offers a way through the difficulty in The Lovers (reversed).

Hopes and Fears · Strength. Strength turns against The Chariot, setting courage against direction: a turning point in the reading. RESONATE's card notes link these two: The Chariot gathers effort toward an aim; Strength asks how the instinct behind that effort is being treated. Progress can combine direction with compassionate limits.

Potential Outcome · The Hermit. After Strength, The Hermit shifts the thread from courage toward reflection.

From new beginnings to reflection, the reading turns 2 times, at Your Approach and Hopes and Fears: those are the places where a card pushes against the one before it, and where choice matters most.

THE OVERALL INVITATION

The themes running through the spread are new beginnings, manipulation, intuition, abundance, authority, tradition, misalignment, direction, courage and reflection. No single element dominates, so the reading reaches across several areas of life at once. The reading is most in tension at Crossing Challenge and Foundation, where the cards in a position pull against each other; that is where your choices count most.

A question to carry, from The Hermit in Potential Outcome: What do I hear in quiet, and when does quiet become a hiding place? This is a perspective, not a fixed prediction.

cardData.name: The Fool
cardData.upright: The Fool is the moment before experience hardens into certainty: openness, curiosity and the courage to move without needing every answer first. Upright, it favours a fresh beginning approached with alertness rather than fear. In a reading, this may describe a new chapter, an unfamiliar choice, or the feeling that life is asking you to move before every detail is known. In a Past position it can reflect the leap that brought you here; in the Present, a threshold you are standing at now; in the Future, an emerging possibility rather than a guaranteed event.
cardData.reversed: Reversed, the same openness can become either careless risk or fear disguised as caution. The question is not simply whether to leap, but whether you are seeing the ground clearly enough to choose freely. Depending on its position and surrounding cards, this may point to hesitation after an earlier risk, or invite a little more preparation before moving forward.

cardData.name: The Magician
cardData.upright: The Magician is focused agency. Knowledge, language, skill and timing are brought together so that intention can become action. Upright, it is less about wishing and more about using what is already available with precision. In a reading, this may be asking what you can actually do with the resources in front of you. In a Past position it can describe an initiative or skill that set events in motion; in the Present, a moment to act consciously; in the Future, developing capability or an opportunity to put intention into practice.
cardData.reversed: Reversed, skill may be scattered, misdirected or used to control rather than create. It can also show ability that is present but not yet trusted. The task is to bring intention, ethics and action back into alignment. Surrounding cards can help distinguish between a temporary lack of confidence, scattered energy, and a situation where motives deserve a closer look.

cardData.name: The High Priestess
cardData.upright: The High Priestess asks for receptivity rather than force. Upright, she points to intuition, silence, pattern recognition and information that becomes visible only when the mind stops trying to dominate the answer. In a reading, this may suggest that not everything needs to be decided immediately. In a Past position it can point to something sensed before it was understood; in the Present, an invitation to listen beneath the noise; in the Future, information or understanding that may unfold gradually rather than arrive all at once.
cardData.reversed: Reversed, the inner signal may be obscured by anxiety, projection or secrecy. It can also suggest that something known inwardly is being ignored because it is inconvenient to the conscious story. Rather than assuming deception, look to the position and surrounding cards for whether the issue is external uncertainty or difficulty trusting your own perception.

cardData.name: The Empress
cardData.upright: The Empress represents life that grows when it is nourished. Upright, she speaks to creativity, embodiment, pleasure, care and the practical conditions that allow something living to flourish. In a reading, this may describe a relationship, project, home, creative impulse or part of yourself asking for genuine nourishment. In a Past position it can show what helped something grow; in the Present, what needs care now; in the Future, growth that may become possible when the right conditions are tended.
cardData.reversed: Reversed, nurturing can become depletion, control or neglect of the self. Creative energy may feel blocked because the environment around it is underfed. Restoration begins with attention to what actually sustains life. The surrounding cards may show whether this is about overgiving to others, neglecting your own needs, or allowing something to rest before expecting it to produce again.

cardData.name: The Emperor
cardData.upright: The Emperor is the capacity to create order that protects what matters. Upright, he represents boundaries, leadership, consistency and the willingness to make decisions that give a system strength. In a reading, this may describe your own need for structure or the influence of someone carrying strong leadership, authority or Aries-like qualities. In a Past position it can point to structures or authority that shaped the situation; in the Present, a need for clear boundaries or decisions; in the Future, greater stability that may come through deliberate organisation rather than prediction of a fixed outcome.
cardData.reversed: Reversed, structure can harden into domination or become so brittle that it no longer serves life. It may also show a lack of dependable boundaries. The question is whether authority is supporting growth or merely defending itself. Position and surrounding cards can help show whether this reflects another person, an institution, or your own relationship with control and responsibility.

cardData.name: The Hierophant
cardData.upright: A teacher, tradition or shared practice can give your experience a useful framework. Learn the reasons behind the rules, then decide which values you want to carry into daily life.
cardData.reversed: Inherited rules may no longer fit your experience. Question a teaching without dismissing everything it offered; distinguish an honest search for meaning from obedience motivated by fear.

cardData.name: The Lovers
cardData.upright: A meaningful relationship or choice asks you to act in line with your values. Mutual openness matters more than an ideal image of harmony; choose the commitments you can honestly sustain.
cardData.reversed: Attraction, duty and personal values may be pulling in different directions. Name the disagreement before promising unity, and avoid sacrificing your voice merely to keep a connection intact.

cardData.name: The Chariot
cardData.upright: Progress depends on bringing competing impulses into a chosen direction. Define what success means, keep your attention on the task, and let discipline coordinate the effort rather than intensify conflict.
cardData.reversed: Pushing harder may conceal uncertainty about where you are going. Reconcile conflicting priorities, check whether the goal is still yours, and regain direction before demanding more speed.

cardData.name: Strength
cardData.upright: Meet a strong feeling or difficult situation with patient courage. Firmness can be gentle: recognise the instinct beneath the reaction and respond without humiliating yourself or another person.
cardData.reversed: Fear, fatigue or harsh self-judgement may make a situation feel unmanageable. Reduce the strain before testing your endurance again; courage can begin with asking for support.

cardData.name: The Hermit
cardData.upright: Step back from competing voices long enough to recognise your own understanding. Solitude, study or a trusted guide can help you identify the next honest step without needing the whole path illuminated.
cardData.reversed: Reflection may have become a way to postpone contact or action. Ask whether solitude is restoring your perspective or protecting you from the conversation you need to have.

cardData.name: Wheel of Fortune
cardData.upright: Circumstances are moving through a turn in the cycle. Notice what is changing beyond your control and use the choices still available; an opening becomes useful when preparation meets timing.
cardData.reversed: A setback or recurring pattern may be exposing the limits of control. Look for the part you can change without blaming yourself for every turn of circumstance.

cardData.name: Justice

cardData.reversed: Something may be obscured by bias, avoidance or an unequal standard. Revisit the facts and hear the missing perspective before deciding what a fair repair would involve.

cardData.name: The Hanged Man
cardData.upright: A deliberate pause can reveal what effort has obscured. Try looking from another position, release the demand for an immediate result, and distinguish useful waiting from giving away your agency.
cardData.reversed: Waiting may have lost its purpose, or a sacrifice may no longer serve anyone. Name what you are postponing and what would make the pause a conscious choice again.

cardData.name: Ace of Cups
cardData.upright: A new feeling or opportunity for connection asks for receptivity. Offer care without demanding an immediate outcome, and notice what replenishes your capacity to give as well as receive.
cardData.reversed: Feelings may be held back or your capacity to care may be depleted. Create a little room to feel privately before expecting yourself to offer more.

cardData.name: Death
cardData.upright: An ending or change of form asks you to release what has completed its purpose. Make room to grieve and attend to what remains alive; this card speaks symbolically of transition, not a prediction of physical death.
cardData.reversed: Holding tightly to an exhausted arrangement may prolong uncertainty. Ask what you fear losing, then consider a smaller, supported act of release rather than forcing yourself to change all at once.

cardData.name: Temperance
cardData.upright: Bring different needs into a workable relationship through measured adjustments. The useful balance is responsive rather than fixed: combine what helps, leave room for rest, and allow integration to take time.
cardData.reversed: An extreme response or impatient mixture may be increasing strain. Simplify the demands, identify what is out of proportion, and rebuild a rhythm you can maintain.

cardData.name: The Devil
cardData.upright: A habit, agreement or desire may be narrowing your sense of choice. Look honestly at its rewards and costs, especially where shame keeps it hidden; begin with one boundary you can actually keep.
cardData.reversed: A binding pattern may be becoming easier to recognise or loosen. Support that awareness with practical changes and help where needed; insight alone does not have to carry the whole recovery.

cardData.name: Two of Wands
cardData.upright: You have an initial foothold and can now consider a wider horizon. Compare the real demands of possible paths and make a plan that allows ambition to meet your circumstances.
cardData.reversed: You may be holding possibilities without choosing, or shrinking a wish to avoid uncertainty. Name the risk you can accept and the information you still need.

cardData.name: The Tower
cardData.upright: A sudden change or unwelcome truth may expose a structure that could not hold. Attend first to immediate support and practical needs, then decide what deserves rebuilding on more honest foundations.
cardData.reversed: You may sense instability while trying to prevent any visible change. Take the warning signs seriously and make manageable repairs rather than waiting until the strain demands an emergency response.

cardData.name: The Star
cardData.upright: After strain, a quieter sense of possibility can return. Replenish what has been depleted and give a modest hope some daily attention; renewal does not require pretending that the difficulty never happened.
cardData.reversed: Hope may feel remote because you are tired or comparing your recovery with an ideal. Seek a reliable source of nourishment and notice small signs of connection before demanding confidence.

cardData.name: Page of Pentacles

cardData.reversed: Planning may be replacing practice or the goal may be too vague to start. Choose one concrete task and learn from doing it before expanding the ambition.

1 · THE ORIGINAL CARD IN THIS POSITION
Original Card · 0 · The Fool

Present Situation

CARD CORRESPONDENCE
Uranus
SKY AT THIS READING
Uranus is at 4° 26′ Gemini

Astrology: Uranus · Air

Number: 0

Zero is pure potential: the circle before the first mark, the unformed field from which every number emerges. In a reading it can amplify openness, uncertainty and the possibility of beginning again.

New Beginnings
Innocence
Trust

Position: Present Situation — The Fool. Here, a willingness to begin before every answer is known is a lens for the central situation as you experience it now. Identify one concrete example in your situation and consider how it shapes your response.

The Fool is the moment before experience hardens into certainty: openness, curiosity and the courage to move without needing every answer first. Upright, it favours a fresh beginning approached with alertness rather than fear. In a reading, this may describe a new chapter, an unfamiliar choice, or the feeling that life is asking you to move before every detail is known. In a Past position it can reflect the leap that brought you here; in the Present, a threshold you are standing at now; in the Future, an emerging possibility rather than a guaranteed event.

Looking closer: Notice the white rose and the bright sky. The rose invites sincerity of intention while the bright sky suggests room to think clearly before stepping ahead.
positions.clar1:
2 · CLARIFIER 1 · HOW IT MODIFIES THE ORIGINAL CARD
Clarifier 1 · X · Wheel of Fortune

Circumstances are moving through a turn in the cycle. Notice what is changing beyond your control and use the choices still available; an opening becomes useful when preparation meets timing.

Astrology: Jupiter · Fire

Number: 10

Ten completes a cycle and carries its consequences into another beginning. In Wheel of Fortune, consider how this relates to change.

Looking closer: A great wheel turns among symbolic creatures while figures rise and fall around it. Movement and recurrence sit alongside the search for enduring understanding.

Wheel of Fortune supports The Fool.

In Present Situation, the theme of change and cycles can help new beginnings and innocence find a constructive outlet.

Read this way because Air and Fire are friendly elements.
positions.clar2:
3 · CLARIFIER 2 · HOW IT DEVELOPS THE RELATIONSHIP BETWEEN BOTH
Clarifier 2 · XI · Justice

Look carefully at evidence, agreements and consequences. A balanced decision requires honesty about your own part as well as the other side; make the choice you can explain and take responsibility for.

Astrology: Libra · Air

Number: 11

Eleven asks for conscious judgement as an established order is examined. In Justice, consider how this relates to fairness.

Looking closer: A seated figure holds scales and an upright sword. Consideration and clear judgement must work together, with consequences following the decision.

Justice reinforces The Fool and supports Wheel of Fortune.

In Present Situation, it draws the original card and the first clarifier together: the theme of fairness and accountability gives new beginnings (The Fool) and change (Wheel of Fortune) a shared direction.

Read this way because with The Fool: both are Air cards; with Wheel of Fortune: Fire and Air are friendly elements.

Clarifier 2 was drawn because Clarifier 1 is also a Major Arcana card (Chas's teaching rule).
positions.notes: The original card and both clarifiers are Major Arcana cards, so a Clarity card is due: one card drawn at random from the unused Minor Arcana, to show where this lands in everyday life (Chas's teaching rule). When it is drawn, this reading updates to include it.
positions.together:
4 · WHAT THEY MEAN TOGETHER
Together in Present Situation

Revision 2 · updated when Clarifier 2 was drawn. The original card and Clarifier 1 readings above are unchanged.

The Fool sets the theme in Present Situation: new beginnings and innocence. Wheel of Fortune gives it somewhere to go, putting new beginnings to use through change. Justice brings them together: through fairness, new beginnings and change point the same way. What is active now is new beginnings, with real momentum behind it from change and fairness. This is the clearest current in this part of the reading.

In the wider Celtic Cross, Present Situation is read with Crossing Challenge, The Magician (reversed; clarified): together they show the situation and what crosses it. There, The Magician modifies The Fool (both are Air cards, but The Magician is reversed).

This is a perspective for reflection, not a fixed prediction.

1 · THE ORIGINAL CARD IN THIS POSITION
Original Card · I · The Magician, reversed

Crossing Challenge

CARD CORRESPONDENCE
Mercury
SKY AT THIS READING
Mercury is at 9° 07′ Scorpio

Astrology: Mercury · Air

Number: 1

One is the first point of definition: identity, initiative and directed force. It is the movement from possibility into a chosen line of action.

Manipulation
Scattered Will
Untapped Skill

Position: Crossing Challenge — The Magician reversed. The tension to explore is scattered effort, unused ability or attempts to control the result. Ask where this pattern becomes difficult and what small adjustment would help you meet it differently.

Reversed, skill may be scattered, misdirected or used to control rather than create. It can also show ability that is present but not yet trusted. The task is to bring intention, ethics and action back into alignment. Surrounding cards can help distinguish between a temporary lack of confidence, scattered energy, and a situation where motives deserve a closer look.

Looking closer: Notice the red outer garment, white clothing and tools on the table. Passion and deliberate effort meet a question of honest purpose: what resources can be used well?
positions.clar1:
2 · CLARIFIER 1 · HOW IT MODIFIES THE ORIGINAL CARD
Clarifier 1 · XII · The Hanged Man

A deliberate pause can reveal what effort has obscured. Try looking from another position, release the demand for an immediate result, and distinguish useful waiting from giving away your agency.

Astrology: Water · Water

Number: 12

Twelve marks a pause in the usual sequence and the possibility of a changed perspective. In The Hanged Man, consider how this relates to perspective.

Looking closer: A figure hangs by one foot with a calm face and a halo. Physical inversion becomes an image of changed perception rather than defeat.

The Hanged Man modifies The Magician (reversed).

In Crossing Challenge, the theme of perspective and surrender changes how manipulation and scattered will may be expressed, rather than strengthening or opposing it.

Read this way because Air and Water are neutral to each other.

Because The Hanged Man is upright, it may show a way through the difficulty shown by The Magician reversed.
positions.clar2:
3 · CLARIFIER 2 · HOW IT DEVELOPS THE RELATIONSHIP BETWEEN BOTH
Clarifier 2 · I · Ace of Cups

A new feeling or opportunity for connection asks for receptivity. Offer care without demanding an immediate outcome, and notice what replenishes your capacity to give as well as receive.

Astrology: Water · Cups · Water

Number: 1

One begins a cycle with a seed, focus or initial act. In Ace of Cups, consider how this relates to openness.

Looking closer: A hand presents an overflowing cup above water, with a dove descending toward it.

Ace of Cups modifies The Magician (reversed) and reinforces The Hanged Man.

In Crossing Challenge, it adds a further angle: the theme of openness and compassion shifts how manipulation (The Magician) and perspective (The Hanged Man) work together.

Read this way because with The Magician: Air and Water are neutral to each other; with The Hanged Man: both are Water cards.

As a Minor Arcana card, Ace of Cups brings the Major theme down to a practical, everyday expression in feelings and relationships.

Clarifier 2 was drawn because Clarifier 1 is also a Major Arcana card (Chas's teaching rule).
positions.together:
4 · WHAT THEY MEAN TOGETHER
Together in Crossing Challenge

Revision 2 · updated when Clarifier 2 was drawn. The original card and Clarifier 1 readings above are unchanged.

The Magician (reversed) sets the theme in Crossing Challenge: manipulation and scattered will. The Hanged Man changes its emphasis, bringing perspective into manipulation. Ace of Cups sides with The Hanged Man, carrying perspective forward through openness and asking what in manipulation has to change. The obstacle here is manipulation giving way to perspective, with openness pushing that change on. The way through is to let perspective change how you hold manipulation. With The Magician reversed, the theme itself is under strain, and The Hanged Man and Ace of Cups show where it can be steadied.

This is a perspective for reflection, not a fixed prediction.

1 · THE ORIGINAL CARD IN THIS POSITION
Original Card · II · The High Priestess

Foundation

CARD CORRESPONDENCE
The Moon
SKY AT THIS READING
Moon is at 18° 30′ Libra

Astrology: The Moon · Water

Number: 2

Two introduces polarity and relationship: self and other, conscious and unconscious, seen and unseen. Wisdom emerges through holding tension rather than collapsing it too quickly.

Intuition
Sacred Mystery
Stillness

Position: Foundation — The High Priestess. Here, patient listening to intuition while allowing missing information to emerge is a lens for the deeper roots beneath the situation. Identify one concrete example in your situation and consider how it shapes your response.

The High Priestess asks for receptivity rather than force. Upright, she points to intuition, silence, pattern recognition and information that becomes visible only when the mind stops trying to dominate the answer. In a reading, this may suggest that not everything needs to be decided immediately. In a Past position it can point to something sensed before it was understood; in the Present, an invitation to listen beneath the noise; in the Future, information or understanding that may unfold gradually rather than arrive all at once.

Looking closer: Notice the blue garment and contrasting pillars. Reflection and deeper understanding sit between opposing possibilities, inviting patience with uncertainty.
positions.clar1:
2 · CLARIFIER 1 · HOW IT MODIFIES THE ORIGINAL CARD
Clarifier 1 · XIII · Death, reversed

Holding tightly to an exhausted arrangement may prolong uncertainty. Ask what you fear losing, then consider a smaller, supported act of release rather than forcing yourself to change all at once.

Astrology: Scorpio · Water

Number: 13

Thirteen transforms a completed form so that another stage can begin. In Death, consider how this relates to transition.

Looking closer: A skeletal rider passes people of different stations as the sun appears between towers. The scene links unavoidable change with the possibility of another beginning.

Death (reversed) modifies The High Priestess.

In Foundation, the theme of clinging and delayed ending changes how intuition and sacred mystery may be expressed, rather than strengthening or opposing it.

Read this way because both are Water cards, but Death is reversed.

Because Death (reversed) is reversed, it may point to what is blocked, delayed or turned inward in this theme.
positions.clar2:
3 · CLARIFIER 2 · HOW IT DEVELOPS THE RELATIONSHIP BETWEEN BOTH
Clarifier 2 · XIV · Temperance

Bring different needs into a workable relationship through measured adjustments. The useful balance is responsive rather than fixed: combine what helps, leave room for rest, and allow integration to take time.

Astrology: Sagittarius · Fire

Number: 14

Fourteen explores integration through patient adjustment rather than a fixed midpoint. In Temperance, consider how this relates to integration.

Looking closer: An angel pours between two cups with one foot on land and one in water. A path leads toward distant light, suggesting patient integration.

Temperance challenges both The High Priestess and Death (reversed).

In Foundation, it questions both earlier cards: the theme of integration and moderation asks whether intuition (The High Priestess) and clinging (Death) need rethinking.

Read this way because with The High Priestess: Water and Fire are contrary elements; with Death: Water and Fire are contrary elements.

Clarifier 2 was drawn because Clarifier 1 is also a Major Arcana card (Chas's teaching rule).

Together in Foundation

This is a perspective for reflection, not a fixed prediction.

Original Card · III · The Empress

Recent Past

CARD CORRESPONDENCE
Venus
SKY AT THIS READING
Venus is at 23° 51′ Libra

Astrology: Venus · Earth

Number: 3

Three is emergence: a third point created from the relationship between two. It is expression, growth, creativity and the first sense of form becoming fertile.

Abundance
Sensual Pleasure
Nurture

Position: Recent Past — The Empress. This may describe how steady care that gives a relationship, project or part of yourself room to grow shaped the path to your current situation. Consider what you want to carry forward and what belongs to an earlier chapter.

The Empress represents life that grows when it is nourished. Upright, she speaks to creativity, embodiment, pleasure, care and the practical conditions that allow something living to flourish. In a reading, this may describe a relationship, project, home, creative impulse or part of yourself asking for genuine nourishment. In a Past position it can show what helped something grow; in the Present, what needs care now; in the Future, growth that may become possible when the right conditions are tended.

Looking closer: Notice the warm yellow landscape and the green growth around the seated figure. Creativity is supported by attention and balance; growth needs both space and care.
positions.clar1:
2 · CLARIFIER 1 · HOW IT MODIFIES THE ORIGINAL CARD
Clarifier 1 · XV · The Devil

A habit, agreement or desire may be narrowing your sense of choice. Look honestly at its rewards and costs, especially where shame keeps it hidden; begin with one boundary you can actually keep.

Astrology: Capricorn · Earth

Number: 15

Fifteen asks how desire and attachment shape the use of personal power. In The Devil, consider how this relates to attachment.

Looking closer: Two figures stand beneath a horned figure with loose chains around their necks. The scene asks what binds them and what room for movement remains.

The Devil reinforces The Empress.

In Recent Past, the emphasis on abundance and sensual pleasure is strengthened by attachment and awareness; this theme is hard to ignore.

Read this way because both are Earth cards.

3 · CLARIFIER 2 · HOW IT DEVELOPS THE RELATIONSHIP BETWEEN BOTH
Clarifier 2 · II · Two of Wands

You have an initial foothold and can now consider a wider horizon. Compare the real demands of possible paths and make a plan that allows ambition to meet your circumstances.

Astrology: Fire · Wands · Fire

Number: 2

Two brings relationship, polarity and the need to consider another position. In Two of Wands, consider how this relates to planning.

Looking closer: A figure holds a globe between two wands while surveying distant land and sea.

Two of Wands modifies both The Empress and The Devil.

In Recent Past, it adds a further angle: the theme of planning and possibility shifts how abundance (The Empress) and attachment (The Devil) work together.

Read this way because with The Empress: Earth and Fire are neutral to each other; with The Devil: Earth and Fire are neutral to each other.

As a Minor Arcana card, Two of Wands brings the Major theme down to a practical, everyday expression in energy, drive and creative action.

1 · THE ORIGINAL CARD IN THIS POSITION
Original Card · IV · The Emperor

Conscious Focus

CARD CORRESPONDENCE
Aries · Mars
SKY AT THIS READING
Mars is at 21° 36′ Leo

Astrology: Aries · Mars · Fire

Number: 4

Four is foundation: the square, the stable frame, the four directions. It brings containment, reliability and the challenge of balancing stability with flexibility.

Authority
Structure
Boundaries

Position: Conscious Focus — The Emperor. Here, clear boundaries and dependable structure that protect what matters is a lens for your hopes, intentions or conscious priorities. Identify one concrete example in your situation and consider how it shapes your response.

The Emperor is the capacity to create order that protects what matters. Upright, he represents boundaries, leadership, consistency and the willingness to make decisions that give a system strength. In a reading, this may describe your own need for structure or the influence of someone carrying strong leadership, authority or Aries-like qualities. In a Past position it can point to structures or authority that shaped the situation; in the Present, a need for clear boundaries or decisions; in the Future, greater stability that may come through deliberate organisation rather than prediction of a fixed outcome.

Looking closer: Notice the red robes and the firm stone throne. Determination is given form through limits, responsibility and practical structure.

2 · CLARIFIER 1 · HOW IT MODIFIES THE ORIGINAL CARD
Clarifier 1 · XVI · The Tower

A sudden change or unwelcome truth may expose a structure that could not hold. Attend first to immediate support and practical needs, then decide what deserves rebuilding on more honest foundations.

Astrology: Mars · Fire

Number: 16

Sixteen breaks a familiar structure and exposes the foundations beneath it. In The Tower, consider how this relates to disruption.

FROM CARD TO CARD

The reading begins with The Fool in Present Situation and moves toward The Hermit in Potential Outcome.

Crossing Challenge · The Magician, reversed. After The Fool, The Magician (reversed) shifts the thread from new beginnings toward manipulation. Reversed, it shows that next step held back or turned inward.

Recent Past · The Empress. After The High Priestess, The Empress gives intuition somewhere to go, turning it toward abundance. RESONATE's card notes link these two: The Priestess senses what is forming; The Empress gives it body, care and material expression.

Conscious Focus · The Emperor. After The Empress, The Emperor shifts the thread from abundance toward authority. RESONATE's card notes link these two: The Empress grows and nourishes; The Emperor defines and protects. Together they ask what conditions allow something valuable to endure.

Your Approach · The Lovers, reversed. The Lovers (reversed) turns against The Hierophant, setting misalignment against tradition: a turning point in the reading. Reversed, it shows that next step held back or turned inward.

Surrounding Influences · The Chariot. After The Lovers (reversed), The Chariot shifts the thread from misalignment toward direction. Upright, it offers a way through the difficulty in The Lovers (reversed).

Potential Outcome · The Hermit. After Strength, The Hermit shifts the thread from courage toward reflection.

The Fool + Wheel of Fortune + Justice

The Empress + The Devil + Two of Wands

CONSCIOUS FOCUS

cardData.name: The Fool
cardData.upright: The Fool is the moment before experience hardens into certainty: openness, curiosity and the courage to move without needing every answer first. Upright, it favours a fresh beginning approached with alertness rather than fear. In a reading, this may describe a new chapter, an unfamiliar choice, or the feeling that life is asking you to move before every detail is known. In a Past position it can reflect the leap that brought you here; in the Present, a threshold you are standing at now; in the Future, an emerging possibility rather than a guaranteed event.
cardData.reversed: Reversed, the same openness can become either careless risk or fear disguised as caution. The question is not simply whether to leap, but whether you are seeing the ground clearly enough to choose freely. Depending on its position and surrounding cards, this may point to hesitation after an earlier risk, or invite a little more preparation before moving forward.

cardData.name: The Magician
cardData.upright: The Magician is focused agency. Knowledge, language, skill and timing are brought together so that intention can become action. Upright, it is less about wishing and more about using what is already available with precision. In a reading, this may be asking what you can actually do with the resources in front of you. In a Past position it can describe an initiative or skill that set events in motion; in the Present, a moment to act consciously; in the Future, developing capability or an opportunity to put intention into practice.
cardData.reversed: Reversed, skill may be scattered, misdirected or used to control rather than create. It can also show ability that is present but not yet trusted. The task is to bring intention, ethics and action back into alignment. Surrounding cards can help distinguish between a temporary lack of confidence, scattered energy, and a situation where motives deserve a closer look.

cardData.name: The High Priestess
cardData.upright: The High Priestess asks for receptivity rather than force. Upright, she points to intuition, silence, pattern recognition and information that becomes visible only when the mind stops trying to dominate the answer. In a reading, this may suggest that not everything needs to be decided immediately. In a Past position it can point to something sensed before it was understood; in the Present, an invitation to listen beneath the noise; in the Future, information or understanding that may unfold gradually rather than arrive all at once.
cardData.reversed: Reversed, the inner signal may be obscured by anxiety, projection or secrecy. It can also suggest that something known inwardly is being ignored because it is inconvenient to the conscious story. Rather than assuming deception, look to the position and surrounding cards for whether the issue is external uncertainty or difficulty trusting your own perception.

cardData.name: The Empress
cardData.upright: The Empress represents life that grows when it is nourished. Upright, she speaks to creativity, embodiment, pleasure, care and the practical conditions that allow something living to flourish. In a reading, this may describe a relationship, project, home, creative impulse or part of yourself asking for genuine nourishment. In a Past position it can show what helped something grow; in the Present, what needs care now; in the Future, growth that may become possible when the right conditions are tended.
cardData.reversed: Reversed, nurturing can become depletion, control or neglect of the self. Creative energy may feel blocked because the environment around it is underfed. Restoration begins with attention to what actually sustains life. The surrounding cards may show whether this is about overgiving to others, neglecting your own needs, or allowing something to rest before expecting it to produce again.

cardData.name: The Emperor
cardData.upright: The Emperor is the capacity to create order that protects what matters. Upright, he represents boundaries, leadership, consistency and the willingness to make decisions that give a system strength. In a reading, this may describe your own need for structure or the influence of someone carrying strong leadership, authority or Aries-like qualities. In a Past position it can point to structures or authority that shaped the situation; in the Present, a need for clear boundaries or decisions; in the Future, greater stability that may come through deliberate organisation rather than prediction of a fixed outcome.
cardData.reversed: Reversed, structure can harden into domination or become so brittle that it no longer serves life. It may also show a lack of dependable boundaries. The question is whether authority is supporting growth or merely defending itself. Position and surrounding cards can help show whether this reflects another person, an institution, or your own relationship with control and responsibility.

cardData.name: The Hierophant
cardData.upright: A teacher, tradition or shared practice can give your experience a useful framework. Learn the reasons behind the rules, then decide which values you want to carry into daily life.
cardData.reversed: Inherited rules may no longer fit your experience. Question a teaching without dismissing everything it offered; distinguish an honest search for meaning from obedience motivated by fear.

cardData.name: The Lovers
cardData.upright: A meaningful relationship or choice asks you to act in line with your values. Mutual openness matters more than an ideal image of harmony; choose the commitments you can honestly sustain.
cardData.reversed: Attraction, duty and personal values may be pulling in different directions. Name the disagreement before promising unity, and avoid sacrificing your voice merely to keep a connection intact.

cardData.name: The Chariot
cardData.upright: Progress depends on bringing competing impulses into a chosen direction. Define what success means, keep your attention on the task, and let discipline coordinate the effort rather than intensify conflict.
cardData.reversed: Pushing harder may conceal uncertainty about where you are going. Reconcile conflicting priorities, check whether the goal is still yours, and regain direction before demanding more speed.

cardData.name: Strength
cardData.upright: Meet a strong feeling or difficult situation with patient courage. Firmness can be gentle: recognise the instinct beneath the reaction and respond without humiliating yourself or another person.
cardData.reversed: Fear, fatigue or harsh self-judgement may make a situation feel unmanageable. Reduce the strain before testing your endurance again; courage can begin with asking for support.

cardData.name: The Hermit
cardData.upright: Step back from competing voices long enough to recognise your own understanding. Solitude, study or a trusted guide can help you identify the next honest step without needing the whole path illuminated.
cardData.reversed: Reflection may have become a way to postpone contact or action. Ask whether solitude is restoring your perspective or protecting you from the conversation you need to have.

cardData.name: Wheel of Fortune
cardData.upright: Circumstances are moving through a turn in the cycle. Notice what is changing beyond your control and use the choices still available; an opening becomes useful when preparation meets timing.
cardData.reversed: A setback or recurring pattern may be exposing the limits of control. Look for the part you can change without blaming yourself for every turn of circumstance.

cardData.name: Justice
cardData.upright: Look carefully at evidence, agreements and consequences. A balanced decision requires honesty about your own part as well as the other side; make the choice you can explain and take responsibility for.
cardData.reversed: Something may be obscured by bias, avoidance or an unequal standard. Revisit the facts and hear the missing perspective before deciding what a fair repair would involve.

cardData.name: The Hanged Man
cardData.upright: A deliberate pause can reveal what effort has obscured. Try looking from another position, release the demand for an immediate result, and distinguish useful waiting from giving away your agency.
cardData.reversed: Waiting may have lost its purpose, or a sacrifice may no longer serve anyone. Name what you are postponing and what would make the pause a conscious choice again.

cardData.name: Ace of Cups
cardData.upright: A new feeling or opportunity for connection asks for receptivity. Offer care without demanding an immediate outcome, and notice what replenishes your capacity to give as well as receive.
cardData.reversed: Feelings may be held back or your capacity to care may be depleted. Create a little room to feel privately before expecting yourself to offer more.

cardData.name: Death
cardData.upright: An ending or change of form asks you to release what has completed its purpose. Make room to grieve and attend to what remains alive; this card speaks symbolically of transition, not a prediction of physical death.
cardData.reversed: Holding tightly to an exhausted arrangement may prolong uncertainty. Ask what you fear losing, then consider a smaller, supported act of release rather than forcing yourself to change all at once.

cardData.name: Temperance
cardData.upright: Bring different needs into a workable relationship through measured adjustments. The useful balance is responsive rather than fixed: combine what helps, leave room for rest, and allow integration to take time.
cardData.reversed: An extreme response or impatient mixture may be increasing strain. Simplify the demands, identify what is out of proportion, and rebuild a rhythm you can maintain.

cardData.name: The Devil
cardData.upright: A habit, agreement or desire may be narrowing your sense of choice. Look honestly at its rewards and costs, especially where shame keeps it hidden; begin with one boundary you can actually keep.
cardData.reversed: A binding pattern may be becoming easier to recognise or loosen. Support that awareness with practical changes and help where needed; insight alone does not have to carry the whole recovery.

cardData.name: Two of Wands
cardData.upright: You have an initial foothold and can now consider a wider horizon. Compare the real demands of possible paths and make a plan that allows ambition to meet your circumstances.
cardData.reversed: You may be holding possibilities without choosing, or shrinking a wish to avoid uncertainty. Name the risk you can accept and the information you still need.

cardData.name: The Tower
cardData.upright: A sudden change or unwelcome truth may expose a structure that could not hold. Attend first to immediate support and practical needs, then decide what deserves rebuilding on more honest foundations.
cardData.reversed: You may sense instability while trying to prevent any visible change. Take the warning signs seriously and make manageable repairs rather than waiting until the strain demands an emergency response.

cardData.name: The Star
cardData.upright: After strain, a quieter sense of possibility can return. Replenish what has been depleted and give a modest hope some daily attention; renewal does not require pretending that the difficulty never happened.
cardData.reversed: Hope may feel remote because you are tired or comparing your recovery with an ideal. Seek a reliable source of nourishment and notice small signs of connection before demanding confidence.

cardData.name: Page of Pentacles
cardData.upright: Choose a skill or practical goal and approach it as a student. Careful attention to a small task can turn interest into experience and reveal the resources you need next.
cardData.reversed: Planning may be replacing practice or the goal may be too vague to start. Choose one concrete task and learn from doing it before expanding the ambition.

cardData.name: The Moon
cardData.upright: Not everything is clear enough to conclude. Attend to dreams and feelings as information about your experience while checking assumptions against evidence; move carefully through ambiguity instead of mistaking fear for certainty.
cardData.reversed: Something previously obscured may be coming into view, though anxiety can still distort it. Separate what you know, what you imagine and what remains uncertain before choosing your response.

cardData.name: Five of Swords
cardData.upright: A conflict may offer a victory that costs too much in trust or connection. Consider what winning would leave behind, and decide whether a boundary, withdrawal or different conversation better serves your aim.
cardData.reversed: A wish to repair may be emerging, but resentment or unequal responsibility can keep the conflict alive. Seek an honest account before asking everyone to move on.

cardData.name: Six of Cups
cardData.upright: A memory, familiar place or simple kindness can reconnect you with something valuable. Receive its warmth while recognising how your present needs differ from those of an earlier time.
cardData.reversed: Nostalgia may be editing the past or an old role may no longer fit. Keep what was nourishing without asking the present to recreate an earlier chapter exactly.

cardData.name: The Sun
cardData.upright: Clarity, warmth or a shared success can restore your energy. Let yourself enjoy what is working and express it plainly; confidence is strongest when it leaves room for other people to shine too.
cardData.reversed: Joy may be temporarily muted, or enthusiasm may be overlooking an important detail. Lower the pressure to appear happy and check what would support a more grounded sense of confidence.

cardData.name: Judgement
cardData.upright: An honest review of the past can help you answer a new sense of purpose. Recognise what you have learned, make amends where possible, and choose the responsibility you are ready to accept now.
cardData.reversed: Harsh self-criticism or fear of change may be drowning out a useful inner call. Distinguish responsibility from punishment and take one concrete step instead of waiting to feel fully worthy.

cardData.name: The World
cardData.upright: A cycle is reaching a meaningful completion. Recognise the skills and relationships that made it possible, attend to the final details, and let what you have learned inform your next participation in the world.
cardData.reversed: Something remains to be integrated before a chapter can close. Identify the unfinished task or unacknowledged feeling rather than chasing a new beginning that leaves the same loose end behind.

cardData.name: Nine of Pentacles
cardData.upright: Recognise the independence or comfort that patient work has made possible. Enjoy it deliberately and maintain the boundaries and relationships that help your life feel chosen rather than merely productive.
cardData.reversed: Success may feel insecure, isolating or too costly to maintain. Reassess the standard you are trying to sustain and the support you need to enjoy what you have built.

positions.original:
1 · THE ORIGINAL CARD IN THIS POSITION
Original Card · II · Two of Swords

Guidance

CARD CORRESPONDENCE
Air · Swords
SKY AT THIS READING
No planetary placement assigned

Astrology: Air · Swords · Air

Number: 2

Two brings relationship, polarity and the need to consider another position. In Two of Swords, consider how this relates to deliberation.

Deliberation
Stalemate
Boundaries

Position: Guidance — Two of Swords. Your next step is to work consciously with deliberation, stalemate, boundaries. Choose one practical response you can try, then notice whether it helps.

A decision may be held between competing needs. Protect enough quiet to hear both sides, but notice which missing fact or feeling must be acknowledged before a genuine choice is possible.

Looking closer: A blindfolded figure holds crossed swords before water under a crescent moon.
positions.clar1:
2 · CLARIFIER 1 · HOW IT MODIFIES THE ORIGINAL CARD
Clarifier 1 · XVI · The Tower

A sudden change or unwelcome truth may expose a structure that could not hold. Attend first to immediate support and practical needs, then decide what deserves rebuilding on more honest foundations.

Astrology: Mars · Fire

Number: 16

Sixteen breaks a familiar structure and exposes the foundations beneath it. In The Tower, consider how this relates to disruption.

Looking closer: Lightning strikes a crowned tower and figures fall from it. The image shows the collapse of assumed security, without specifying a literal future event.

The Tower supports Two of Swords.

In Guidance, the theme of disruption and revelation can help deliberation and stalemate find a constructive outlet.

Read this way because Air and Fire are friendly elements.

As a Major Arcana card, The Tower suggests a larger life theme behind this everyday situation.
positions.clar2:
3 · CLARIFIER 2 · HOW IT DEVELOPS THE RELATIONSHIP BETWEEN BOTH
Clarifier 2 · XX · Judgement

An honest review of the past can help you answer a new sense of purpose. Recognise what you have learned, make amends where possible, and choose the responsibility you are ready to accept now.

Astrology: Fire · Fire

Number: 20

Twenty reviews the journey and invites a more conscious response to its meaning. In Judgement, consider how this relates to awakening.

Looking closer: Figures rise toward an angel sounding a trumpet. The image suggests a summons to awareness and renewal rather than a final verdict on a person.

Judgement supports Two of Swords and reinforces The Tower.

In Guidance, it draws the original card and the first clarifier together: the theme of awakening and review gives deliberation (Two of Swords) and disruption (The Tower) a shared direction.

Read this way because with Two of Swords: Air and Fire are friendly elements; with The Tower: both are Fire cards.

As a Major Arcana card, Judgement suggests a larger life theme behind this everyday situation.

Clarifier 2 was drawn because Clarifier 1 is a Major Arcana card (Chas's teaching rule).
positions.notes: Clarifier 2 is also a Major Arcana card. The Clarity card applies only when the original card is a Major too, so nothing further is drawn here (at most two clarifiers per card).

4 · WHAT THEY MEAN TOGETHER
Together in Guidance

Revision 2 · updated when Clarifier 2 was drawn. The original card and Clarifier 1 readings above are unchanged.

Two of Swords sets the theme in Guidance: deliberation and stalemate. The Tower gives it somewhere to go, putting deliberation to use through disruption. Judgement brings them together: through awakening, deliberation and disruption point the same way. As guidance, the cards point to deliberation, with real momentum behind it from disruption and awakening. Lean into deliberation: the cards back it.

This is a perspective for reflection, not a fixed prediction.

cardData.name: Two of Swords
cardData.upright: A decision may be held between competing needs. Protect enough quiet to hear both sides, but notice which missing fact or feeling must be acknowledged before a genuine choice is possible.
cardData.reversed: Avoidance or too much information may be making the decision harder. Name the underlying concern and choose a practical next step rather than demanding perfect certainty.

cardData.name: The Tower
cardData.upright: A sudden change or unwelcome truth may expose a structure that could not hold. Attend first to immediate support and practical needs, then decide what deserves rebuilding on more honest foundations.
cardData.reversed: You may sense instability while trying to prevent any visible change. Take the warning signs seriously and make manageable repairs rather than waiting until the strain demands an emergency response.

cardData.name: Judgement
cardData.upright: An honest review of the past can help you answer a new sense of purpose. Recognise what you have learned, make amends where possible, and choose the responsibility you are ready to accept now.
cardData.reversed: Harsh self-criticism or fear of change may be drowning out a useful inner call. Distinguish responsibility from punishment and take one concrete step instead of waiting to feel fully worthy.
